title: CopenScene
problem: Concerts for Copenhagen's metal, hardcore and punk scene are spread over 25 venue websites.
people: Fans of the scene who want one overview, and a reason to check back when a show changes.
build: A scheduled worker scrapes 25 venues into Postgres. It re-reads only concerts whose listing changed, so a daily run takes seconds.
A React client lists the concerts and shows them on a map.
Passwordless accounts mark concerts, and a status change is recorded as an alert.
Decisions are written down as ADRs. The curated venue list is the product's boundary.

title: New Era
problem: Job listings arrive from several sites, and most of them do not fit.
people: A job seeker who wants to read only the jobs worth applying for, without sending a CV to a cloud service.
build: Collects and deduplicates listings from LinkedIn and Jobindex.
A local Ollama model scores each job from 0 to 100 against the CV and shows its reasoning inline.
Jobs appear at once, and scores fill in as the model finishes.
A kanban board tracks applications, with notes and interview dates. Everything runs locally.

title: Citadel
problem: Running a D&D game means juggling prep notes, rules and session logs across many tools.
people: One game master, me, before, during and after each session. It runs on my own server.
build: Campaign content lives in its own git repository, the Vault. The app holds only code.
An MCP server exposes the campaign to an AI assistant through the same core as the HTTP API.
A compendium of monsters, spells and items is imported from a pinned, checksummed 5e.tools release.
Typecheck, lint, unit tests and Playwright end-to-end tests run against a fresh dev Vault.

title: Agent-first CLIs
problem: AI agents use an API most safely through a tool with strict, predictable output.
people: AI agents, and the people who supervise what those agents do.
build: Standard output carries JSON data only. Errors go to standard error as structured JSON.
Typed exit codes separate auth, validation, not found, network and schema drift.
brevo-cli reaches all 291 Brevo API operations and refuses outward actions, such as sending email, until a person approves.
A family of CLIs: Hevy, Brevo, Scryfall, Archidekt, Hardcover, Yazio and Saxo.

title: Game Night
problem: A monthly board game night needs RSVPs, game choices and table plans.
people: A host and their friends, joining from one group link without passwords.
build: Approval voting on suggested games.
A planner picks the games that suit the most attendees and splits large groups into two tables.
The host's shelf is imported from a BoardGameGeek export.

title: Better CardMarket
problem: Building a wants list on Cardmarket takes many manual clicks per card.
people: Magic: The Gathering players who buy singles.
build: Pastes a decklist into a wants list, card by card.
Selects allowed printings by rules and estimates the price of the list.

title: eazy gains
problem: Planning high-protein dinners around this week's grocery offers takes time.
people: One to four people who cook dinner at home in Denmark.
build: Plans three to seven dinners from current offers at five Danish grocery chains.
Fits each dinner to a protein and calorie range, and builds a shopping list per store.
